In under-resolved flows, the unfiltered scheme has no numerical dissipation and accumulates energy at the grid scale. Filtering relieves this accumulation and a larger $α$ gives a more compact spectrum. Long-time simulations reproduce selective decay, including relaxation toward the Arnold-type bound and the inverse cascade of the mean square potential.

papers.title: Morse theory and a degree formula for the resonant singular Paneitz equation on four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We develop Morse theory for the singular Paneitz equation at resonant mass on closed four-manifolds with conical orders between minus one and zero and Paneitz kernel consisting of the constants. Under nondegeneracy of the reduced interactions and nonvanishing of the leading mass-defect coefficients, we classify the critical points at infinity by the sign of these coefficients. We compute their indices and their contributions to the relative homology of sublevels. The topology of very low sublevels is determined by weighted barycenters of strictly smaller total weight and by the negative Paneitz eigenspace. These results yield strong Morse inequalities and a Leray--Schauder degree formula at resonance, which also applies when genuine solutions are degenerate. On the round four-sphere with two conical points, the Morse inequalities give existence on an open set of data for which the degree vanishes.

papers.title: Non-Intrusive Least-Squares Reduced Basis Methods: Black-Box Snapshots and Exact Residual Certificates
papers.abstract: For a parametrized linear first-order system, the least-squares functional at a conforming pair is the squared norm of the residual of the continuous problem, and it can be computed exactly. In this paper, we use this least-squares residual as the error certificate of reduced basis methods whose snapshots are computed by black-box solvers. The output of the solver is first made conforming by a reconstruction, and a flux is recovered by least-squares if the solver does not provide one. The online reduced problem minimizes the least-squares functional over the product of the space spanned by the snapshot fluxes and the space spanned by the snapshot potentials. It needs no inf--sup condition on the reduced spaces, and its certificate needs no stability constant. We discuss second-order elliptic equations, the Stokes equations, where only the velocity of a black-box solver is used, and linear transport equations with a moving inflow boundary. In the numerical experiments, the snapshots are computed by least-squares, conforming, nonconforming, stabilized, finite volume, and finite difference solvers. With adaptive meshes and the same tolerances, the greedy algorithm stops at the same or nearly the same reduced dimension for all solvers that accept a mesh.

papers.title: Stability of separable solutions to a fast diffusion system
papers.abstract: We study a Dirichlet fast diffusion system with symmetric linear cross-loss terms on a bounded smooth domain. A coupled Rayleigh quotient captures the variational structure of the coupling and is nonincreasing along sufficiently regular positive solution pairs. Under the common extinction and regularity hypotheses, this monotonicity and the energy identity yield upper and lower bounds \[ C^{-1}(T^*-t)^{1/(p-1)} \le \|(u(t),v(t))\|_{L^{p+1}(Ω)} \le C(T^*-t)^{1/(p-1)}. \] In the Sobolev subcritical range, a Lyapunov functional for the rescaled system yields a sequence of times $t_j\uparrow T^*$ along which the rescaled pair converges strongly in $H_0^1(Ω)\times H_0^1(Ω)$ to a nonnegative classical stationary solution pair. The integral lower bound excludes the trivial limiting pair, while the coupling with $α>0$ ensures that neither limiting component is identically zero. As a further property of the stationary system, we show that proportional components of a nontrivial nonnegative solution pair must coincide. We also construct a positive diagonal stationary solution pair by constrained minimization. Scalar upper comparison and a Bénilan--Crandall-type estimate for smooth positive diagonal solutions provide complementary links with the scalar fast diffusion equation.

papers.title: On Bramble-Pasciak-type preconditioners and their properties
papers.abstract: Bramble and Pasciak (Math. Comp., 1988) discovered a preconditioning method for linear algebraic systems in saddle point form, which under certain conditions transforms a symmetric indefinite saddle point matrix into a nonsymmetric matrix that is positive definite in some non-standard inner product. Thus, the method "removes" the indefiniteness of the problem, while retaining the property that the preconditioned system can be solved using an optimal Krylov subspace method with three-term recurrences. Since this well-known method has some limitations, several variants with potential improvements have been proposed in the literature. In this paper, we attempt a systematic assessment of the mathematical properties and practical efficiency of Bramble-Pasciak-type preconditioners. Our goal is to close some gaps in the understanding of these techniques. We identify and analyze the three main methods in this context, highlighting a variant that offers additional flexibility but has received little attention to date. We perform detailed spectral analyzes of the preconditioned matrices and illustrate our theoretical results on several numerical examples.

papers.title: The exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation
papers.abstract: We solve the exterior Dirichlet problem for the Weingarten equation of minimal type over the complementary of domains satisfying an interior sphere condition, and investigate some related problems. Namely, by linearizing the Weingarten equation, we give an asymptotic expansion for exterior solutions and we completely identify which classes of Weingarten minimal ends satisfy a maximum principle at infinity. Building on the previous results, we study symmetries of the solutions and questions related to the uniqueness of the solutions.

papers.title: Propagation failure for bistable differential equations on periodic trees
papers.abstract: We study traveling fronts for bistable reaction-diffusion equations on periodic heterogeneous trees. We use comparison principles to estimate the pinning and propagation regions for both cubic and general bistabilities. Our analytical results and numerical simulations show that the interesting propagation reversal effects found in homogeneous trees become more pronounced in the heterogeneous setting, paving the way towards understanding more general graphs. As the diffusion strength increases, the waves end up moving in the same direction irrespective of the bistability. This direction is determined solely by the underlying structure of the heterogeneous tree. Our techniques also lead to sharper results for the homogeneous setting.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Single-Control Null Controllability of Stochastic Heat Equations
papers.abstract: We disprove the conjecture that a single localized drift control suffices for null controllability of stochastic parabolic equations with bounded adapted coefficients. On a bounded interval with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, we construct a deterministic, nonnegative smooth noise coefficient supported at positive distance from the control interval. One fixed nonzero smooth initial state cannot be driven to zero almost surely at any positive time by any progressively measurable control with finite expected $L^2$ energy. The proof uses products of Brownian increments in the adjoint terminal data to keep the initial pairing bounded away from zero while the observation norm tends to zero. On the flat torus, the construction yields counterexamples in every Gevrey class of order $s>1$ whenever the complement of the control set contains an open ball. Thus Gevrey regularity above order one cannot replace analyticity as a general sufficient condition for null controllability.

papers.title: Critical exponents and near-critical limits for random matrix products
papers.abstract: We study the approach to the zero-Lyapunov-exponent transition for products of independent, identically distributed invertible matrices. The matrix laws are supported in a common compact subset of $GL(d,\mathbb{R})$ and converge in total variation to a strongly irreducible and proximal law with zero top Lyapunov exponent. We establish a near-critical renewal theorem for the occupation measure and a functional diffusion limit for the logarithmic cocycle as well as exact asymptotics and scaling limits for three observables describing the transient dynamics. The expected number of escapes from the unit ball and the expected number of visits to a fixed annulus diverge as the inverse absolute Lyapunov exponent, and both counts have exponential limits after normalization. The time spent on the side opposite to the asymptotic drift has critical exponent two and converges, after rescaling, to the positive occupation time of Brownian motion with negative drift.

papers.title: CLT for Linear Spectral Statistics of sample covariances of superimposition of Separable Covariance Components
papers.abstract: Suppose $\{Z_r\}_{r=1}^K$ are $p\times n$ random matrices with entries having zero mean and unit variance and $p/n \to c \in (0,\infty)$. We construct the sample covariance matrix $S_n = \frac{1}{n}XX^*$ where $X =\sum_{r=1}^K X_r$, where $X_r = A_r^\frac{1}{2}Z_rB_r^\frac{1}{2}$, $K \in \mathbb{N}$ and $A_r,B_r$ are sequences of positive semi-definite matrices of dimensions $p\times p$ and $n\times n$, respectively that are are simultaneously digaonalizable within themselves. As an extension of our previous work related to the L.S.D. of such classes of matrices, we show that the linear spectral statistics arising from the spectra of $S_n$ have Gaussian limits under assumptions of fourth moment bounds on the entries of $\{Z_r\}_{r=1}^K$ and convergence of the joint spectral distribution of $\{A_r\}_{r=1}^K$ and $\{B_r\}_{r=1}^K$ to probability distributions over $\mathbb{R}_+^K$ with compact support.

papers.title: Generic bi-stochastic semigroups are flows
papers.abstract: We demonstrate genericity wrt. the weak polynomial topology of the space $\mathrm{Aut}(X, μ)$ of invertible measure-preserving transformations within the space of bi-stochastic operators over $L^{2}(X, μ)$ for standard probability spaces $(X, μ)$. This improves upon the approximation and residuality results established by Brown [4] and Kim [26] (cf. also [16]). We make crucial use of a reformulation of the Birkhoff--von Neumann theorem [2, 43] due to Kim for bi-stochastic operators over infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces. This enables the construction of stochastic processes, via which dilations and thereby $\mathrm{PW}$-approximations may be obtained. In a similar fashion, we demonstrate the weak-genericity of weakly-continuous measure-preserving flows on $(X, μ)$ within the space of $\mathcal{C}_{0}$-semigroups of bi-stochastic operators on $L^{2}(X, μ)$. To achieve this, we make use of random measures (viz. Poisson point processes) and build on our discrete-time result. This complements recent advances in ergodic theory due to Furlong on the genericity of measure-preserving flows in the space of measure-preserving semi-flows.

papers.title: Variational Principles and Machine Learning: a Numerical Analysis and PDE perspective
papers.abstract: Variational principles have played a fundamental role in the development of modern mathematics, physics, and scientific computing. From the principles of least action in mechanics to the calculus of variations and the variational formulation of partial differential equations, they have provided a powerful framework for understanding complex problems and designing reliable numerical methods. In recent years, Machine Learning has introduced a new computational paradigm, in which highly expressive nonlinear function spaces and large-scale minimisation problems play a central role. In these notes, we explore the connection between these two frameworks. We develop a variational and numerical-analysis perspective on Machine Learning algorithms, focusing in particular on their formulation as nonlinear minimisation problems. We investigate how classical concepts such as stability, consistency, approximability, and compactness acquire new interpretations in this setting, and how the variational structure of the underlying continuous problem can govern the behaviour of neural-network approximations. This perspective provides a mathematical framework for understanding existing ML algorithms while also suggesting new approaches to their design. In particular, alternative and strongly coercive variational principles can lead to more stable, reliable, and potentially more efficient computational methods.

papers.title: Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements
papers.abstract: The inverse problem of identifying spatially varying material properties of heterogeneous solids using experimentally available displacement fields and boundary reaction forces alone remains challenging. Being able to characterize heterogeneous and graded solids would be advantageous in the design and manufacturing of functionally graded materials and composites. Additionally, an efficient technique for identifying heterogeneous material properties from in vivo measurements would be useful in biomedical contexts to characterize heterogeneous biological tissues. Although several techniques developed over the past two decades have addressed inverse identification for homogeneous materials, including linear elastic, hyperelastic, viscoelastic, and elastoplastic solids, comparatively fewer studies have considered heterogeneous and graded materials. Furthermore, several recent approaches to characterizing heterogeneous and graded materials employ parameter-heavy, deep learning-based frameworks trained to enforce force equilibrium at specified collocation points within the material. In this work, we propose an interpretable and time-efficient framework that predicts the three-dimensional relative spatial variation of a constitutive parameter field for multiple parameters of a heterogeneous hyperelastic material, using only displacement-field data. In this work, we validate our framework on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks involving heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials. By leveraging the linear nature of the inverse problem for hyperelastic materials and directly optimizing for the constitutive parameters at the finite-element level, we achieve acceptable prediction accuracy with significantly lower computational time compared to recently reported deep-learning-based frameworks.

papers.title: Measurable equidecomposability and the Banach--Ruziewicz problem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields
papers.abstract: We prove a measurable analogue of the Banach--Tarski paradox over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields. Let $\mathbb K$ be the completion of a number field at a non-Archimedean place (e.g., $\mathbb K=\mathbb Q_p$) and $n\ge 2$. Then any two bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$ with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure can be cut into finitely many Haar measurable pieces and rearranged into each other by elements of a certain countable group $Γ$ of affine isometries. We also show that the Haar measure is, up to a constant factor, the unique nonzero finitely additive $Γ$-invariant measure on the bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$, which solves a $p$-adic version of the Banach--Ruziewicz problem. Both results follow from the fact that the action of $Γ$ on $\mathbb K^n$ is expanding, a property closely related to the spectral gap. For $n=1$ and arbitrary characteristic, we obtain analogous results when the residue field is not prime, using a countable group of isometries that are not necessarily affine.

papers.title: A Joint Functional Central Limit Theorem for the $L^p$-Norm Profile of Random Littlewood Polynomials
papers.abstract: For a random Littlewood polynomial $q_n(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\varepsilon_jz^j$ with independent Rademacher coefficients, let $S_n(θ)=|q_n(e^{iθ})|^2/n$ be its normalized angular intensity. Its positive moments $T_n^{(p)}=\|q_n\|_p^p/n^{p/2}$ form the moment profile of the intensity distribution under normalized arc measure on the unit circle. We prove a joint functional central limit theorem for this profile. For $p$ in a compact interval $K\subset(0,\infty)$ and logarithmic time $n=\lfloor Ne^t\rfloor$, $t\in[-T,T]$, the piecewise linear interpolations of $\sqrt n(T_n^{(p)}-Γ(1+p/2))$ converge to a Gaussian field $G(p,t)$ in $C(K\times[-T,T])$. The corresponding step processes converge in $D([-T,T];C(K))$ with the Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. The limit has the representation $G(p,t)=\sum_{a=2}^{\infty}c_a(p)G^{(a)}(t)$, where $c_a(p)$ are the ordinary Laguerre coefficients of $x^{p/2}$, with $L_a(0)=1$. The independent centered stationary Gaussian modes have covariance $\mathrm{Cov}(G^{(a)}(s),G^{(a)}(t))=2V_a e^{-(a-1/2)|t-s|}$, where $V_a$ is the squared $L^2$-norm of the density of the sum of $a$ independent uniform random variables on $[0,1]$. We also obtain the functional limit theorem for $\|q_n\|_p/\sqrt n$ and identify its joint covariance. At $p=4$, we recover the known scalar autocorrelation fluctuation law and identify its dependence across nested lengths. Finite-mode convergence follows from the multivariate functional de Jong theorem after model-specific variance, influence, and fourth-moment calculations. Maximal estimates control the infinite Laguerre tail and its exponent derivative uniformly over nested lengths.

papers.title: Converse comparison of $g$-expectations and uniqueness of generators of BSDEs: a novel approach and some sharp results
papers.abstract: This paper investigates inverse problems for backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs), with a particular focus on the converse comparison theorem and the uniqueness of generators solely through the initial values of the corresponding solutions. To this end, we develop a forward-SDE representation approach that combines a contradiction argument with a representation of generators in terms of solutions to associated forward stochastic differential equations (SDEs). As one of the main consequences, we prove that an ordering between two $g$-expectations necessarily implies the pointwise comparability of their generators, without requiring any additional structural assumptions beyond the standard Lipschitz condition. This removes the continuity, $y$-independence, and deterministic assumptions required in previous works, thereby yielding a complete solution to the converse comparison problem for $g$-expectations under the standard Lipschitz framework and, at the same time, establishing a general uniqueness theorem for generators of BSDEs.

papers.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
papers.abstract:
We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted. We construct the thermodynamic limit of the electron gas with constant total density and a prescribed SSW magnetization. Its energy per unit volume $e_{m SSW}$ is evaluated at the local wavevector $
abla\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the spiral phase. When $\varphi$ is the azimuthal angle of the magnetization $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,m_2,m_3)$, the approximation reads \[ E(ρ,\mathbf{m})\approx\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}e_{m SSW} ig(ρ(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{x}),
abla\varphi(\mathbf{x}) ig)\,d \mathbf{x}. \] Here $
abla\varphi$ measures the local rotation of $\mathbf{m}$ about the third axis. Wherever $m_1^2+m_2^2>0$, it equals $(m_1
abla m_2-m_2
abla m_1)/(m_1^2+m_2^2)$. The approximation thus depends only on the total density $ρ$, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the spin-polarized density in the rotating frame and the local wavevector vary on the length scale $N^{1/3}$, with $N$ the mean number of particles, we obtain an error $O(N^{5/6})$ for an energy of order $N$. Setting the phase to zero gives the noncollinear local spin density approximation (LSDA) for arbitrary magnetization directions.

papers.title: A Short Proof of the Goldman--Parker Conjecture
papers.abstract: Goldman and Parker conjectured that the three order-two complex side reflections of an ideal triangle with Cartan angular invariant $A$ define a discrete and faithful representation of $\mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2$ in $PU(2,1)$ whenever $\tan^2 A\le 125/3$. Schwartz first proved the conjecture using rigorous computer-assisted estimates and later gave an analytic proof based on three loxodromic $\mathbb R$-spheres. We give a substantially shorter proof of this conjecture using a simpler geometric construction. For parameters just below the critical value, we use the Cygan bisector of the two fixed points of the triple product of the reflections. This wall and one of its cusp translates bound a strip from which we construct a trapping region. At the critical value $\tan^2 A=125/3$, the two fixed points merge, and the same construction applies to the limiting wall.

papers.title: Extremals and Normalized Solutions for a Critical Weighted Choquard Equation
papers.abstract: We study normalized solutions to the weighted Choquard equation \[ \left\{ \begin{aligned} -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u) &=λ|x|^{-2a}u+β|x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u\\ &\quad+|x|^{-bp} \left( \int_{\mathbb R^N} \frac{|u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^μ|y|^{bp}}\,dy \right) |u|^{p-2}u &&\text{in }\mathbb R^N,\\ \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx&=ρ^2, \end{aligned} \right. \] where $N\ge3$, $a<(N-2)/2$, $a<b<a+1$, $2<q<2^\sharp$, $0<μ<N$, $p=(2N-μ)/(N-2d)$ is the upper Stein--Weiss critical exponent, $d=1-b+a$, $2^\sharp=2N/(N-2-2a+2b)$, $ρ>0$ is prescribed, $β>0$, and $λ\in\mathbb R$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplier. Assuming $p>2$, we establish existence and multiplicity of normalized solutions in different mass regimes, including negative-energy ground states for small $β$ and positive-energy second solutions under suitable assumptions, as well as ground states in the mass-critical and mass-supercritical cases under explicit conditions

papers.title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
papers.abstract: We establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. For small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. Both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

papers.title: Global well-posedness for the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation in the one-dimensional Zhidkov space
papers.abstract: We show global well-posedness for the focusing Gross-Pitaevskii equation in one spatial dimension, with initial data in the Zhidkov space, with no smallness condition. For the usual nonlinear Schrödinger equation with decaying initial data, a mass-energy argument is used to preclude finite-time blow-up. Here both mass and total energy are infinite, but we put together a renormalized version of that bound by using the net mass transfer and the kinetic energy, which we show are a priori bounded. Global well-posedness on the energy space and on $1+H^1$ follows. We also treat a variant of the equation with a smooth real density response to show how this construction can be generalized to different nonlinearities.

papers.title: Mean field game value multifunction: dynamic programming principle
papers.abstract: We study mean field games (MFGs) on the torus with non-degenerate diffusion, in a regime (no monotonicity) where multiple solutions exist for the same data. In this setting the value of a representative player is not a function of the initial time and distribution, and the classical master equation loses its meaning. We describe the dependence of the value on the initial data by a multivalued mapping, the value multifunction, assigning to each initial time and distribution the set of value functions of all solutions of the MFG starting from that data. Our main result gives a sufficient condition for a closed multifunction to be a value multifunction, namely, it must satisfy a dynamic programming principle formulated on proper time subintervals, expressed as invariance of its graph under the forward operators generated by equilibria of the game. This replaces the global requirement that each value be produced by a solution of the forward-backward system on the whole time interval by a local, time-consistent condition together with closedness, which carries the terminal condition. The result is the second-order analogue of the viability approach previously developed for first-order mean field games. We reformulate solutions of the mean field game in terms of relaxed equilibria, show that the closure of a value multifunction is again a value multifunction, and prove that the forward operators compose as a semigroup. We also present an explicit example in which a single terminal cost produces at least two solutions for every initial time in an interval, while solutions are unique for initial times sufficiently close to the horizon.

papers.title: Prophet Inequalities for Mixtures of I.I.D. Random Variables
papers.abstract: A latent index $J\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$ is drawn from a prior $π$. Conditional on $J=j$, a gambler observes random variables $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ drawn independently from a non-negative component distribution $F_j$. The gambler knows $n$, the prior $π$, and the component distributions $F_1,\ldots,F_k$, but not $J$, observes the values sequentially, and selects at most one value at the time it is revealed. We show that the largest $α$ such that the gambler can guarantee to select a value of $α\cdot\mathbb{E}[\max_iX_i]$ in expectation, for all distributions where this expectation is finite, is \[ α=\frac1e+\frac{1}{k^{2/3+o(1)}}. \] The lower bound is achieved by the better of two variants of the standard secretary rule. The upper bound uses a finely tuned instance of the common-scale model, which scales a sequence of independent random variables by a single latent variable.

papers.title: Fundamental Symmetries in Krein Spaces
papers.abstract: We study the space of fundamental symmetries of a real or complex Krein space in finite or infinite dimension. After recalling the equivalence of the associated Hilbert norms, we describe two global operator parametrizations and their relation. The space is realized as a Banach symmetric space under $m(J,J')=JJ'J$. Its canonical connection is the tangential projection of the flat derivative in the real Banach space of Krein-self-adjoint operators. This yields explicit formulas for geodesics, parallel transport, transvections, and curvature. The positive square roots $(JJ')^{1/2}$ implement both isometries between the associated Hilbert spaces and geodesic transvections. A proof of their intertwining property in an earlier publication is corrected.

papers.title: Development of a GPU-accelerated numerical simulation model for liver infection in realistic domains
papers.abstract: Viral hepatitis reduces the functionality of the liver and constitutes a major global health concern because it oftentimes evolves to chronic inflammation leading to long term liver damage. Mathematical models on a mesoscopic scale abstract from only partly known cell-scale processes while providing an in-silico tool for understanding tissue-scale development of the disease. In this work, we investigate the interactions between virus and immune cells in a realistic three-dimensional liver geometries by using a reaction-diffusion model that reproduces infection courses with cure and with chronic developments. A GPU-based finite-difference implementation, released as an open-source Python library, achieves speedups greater than x30 for realistic mesh sizes, making three-dimensional simulations on realistic geometries computationally tractable. This provides a basis for future in-silico studies of treatment strategies, such as testing antiviral or immunomodulatory therapies, and for patient-specific simulations based on individual liver geometries, paving the way towards personalized healthcare.

papers.title: Integrable nearest neighbor interaction Hamiltonians and the rigidity of the Toda Lattice
papers.abstract: We consider mechanical Hamiltonian systems, where the potentials describe a nearest-neighbor interaction law. In this setting, a non trivial example of an integrable system is the celebrated Toda lattice. We study deformations of this potential (for three particles), and show that some classes of analytic deformations of the potential break its integrability, without assuming anything about the form of the integrals. This result is reminiscent of local rigidity of ellipses in billiards. The proof relies on the fact that high energy orbits for the Toda lattice approximate billiard orbits in some polytopes.

papers.title: Polynomial-degree-robust saturation on triangular meshes
papers.abstract: We prove a polynomial-degree-robust ($p$-robust) saturation property for conforming finite element approximations of the Poisson equation on shape-regular triangular meshes. Previously, a $p$-robust saturation estimate for the spectral method on a square was proved in [C. Canuto et al., A saturation property for the spectral-Galerkin approximation of a Dirichlet problem in a square, ESAIM Math. Model. Numer. Anal., 53 (2019), pp. 987--1003]. For every fixed $λ>1$, increasing the polynomial degree from $p$ to any $q\geq\lceilλp\rceil+3$ reduces the energy error by a factor $α_λ\in(0,1)$ independent of $p$ and the mesh size, up to a data oscillation term.

papers.title: Weak-strong stability and uniqueness of measure-valued solutions to (nonlocal) pressureless Euler-type systems
papers.abstract: We consider the pressureless Euler equation possibly coupled with non-local forces like the Poisson and alignment interactions. We overcome the lack of strict convexity in the relative entropy inequality that arises from the lack of pressure. The key to this result is the appropriate framework of the solution scheme utilizing the generalized Young measure which yields extra structural properties for the oscillation and concentration parts of the measure-valued solution. We overcome the problem of density mismatch via two complementary techniques. The first takes advantage of a Figalli--Kang-type transport inequality. The second involves establishing a generation lemma for the generalized Young measure which simultaneously establishes $L^2$-based control in flat metric between the measure-valued density and the density generating sequence.

papers.title: The capillary $L_{p}$ dual Christoffel-Minkowski-type problem for $p\geq q$ with $1\leq k\leq n$
papers.abstract:
We study the following fully nonlinear $k$-Hessian equation on a spherical cap $\mathcal{C}_θ$ for $1\leq k\leq n$ and $0<θ<π/2$: $$ \left\{  egin{aligned} σ_k(
abla^2h+hσ) &=fh^{p-1} igl(h^2+|
abla h|^2 igr)^{ rac{k+1-q}{2}} &&	ext{in }\mathcal{C}_θ,\

In the critical case $p=q>1$, scaling invariance prevents uniform $C^0$ estimates without normalization. We overcome this difficulty using a logarithmic gradient estimate and a normalized approximation with uniqueness up to dilation.

papers.title: The confined discrete DLSS equation: gradient flow structure and long-time asymptotics
papers.abstract: We propose and analyse a structure-preserving discretization of the fourth-order DLSS equation in dynamically rescaled variables leading to a linear confinement on the one-dimensional real line. The scheme is obtained as a discrete analogue of the Carrillo--Toscani splitting. It allows for a new interpretation of the DLSS equation as gradient flow of the relative entropy with respect to a combined diffusive and transport metric, extending the structure of the discretization introduced in our earlier work with Giuseppe Savaré for the unconfined equation. We prove global existence of positive solutions and, as the main analytical result, exponential decay of the relative entropy towards the discrete Gaussian equilibrium. The decay rate is obtained via a discrete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. The resulting rate is consistent with the continuum rate and converges to it from below in the vanishing mesh-size limit. Numerical results illustrate and confirm our findings.

papers.title: Generic non-convergence of low-temperature Ising Glauber dynamics on $\mathbb Z^2$
papers.abstract: We study how typical convergence is, in the topological sense of Baire category, for the heat-bath Glauber dynamics of the nearest-neighbour, zero-field Ising model on $\mathbb Z^2$ started from translation-invariant initial laws. At sufficiently low positive temperature, we show that the initial laws whose evolution has both the plus and the minus phase as weak subsequential limits form a dense $G_δ$ subset of the space of translation-invariant laws with the weak topology. Consequently, the initial laws for which the dynamics converges in distribution form a meagre set, which gives a partial answer to an open problem posed by Liggett. In particular, a large initial magnetisation does not force convergence to the plus phase, even for spatially ergodic initial laws. The proof combines equilibrium and mixing estimates of Gheissari and Sly with a periodic grid of plus spins of vanishing density and Baire's theorem, and it applies to all reversible monotone Glauber dynamics for the Ising model.

papers.title: Time-consistency of cash-subadditive risk measures: The infimal cocycle property
papers.abstract: We characterize the time-consistency of convex, cash-subadditive dynamic risk measures in terms of their minimal penalty. The dual variables are conditional sub-probability densities, which factorize across an intermediate date in many ways, according to how the discount is allocated to the two periods. We introduce an infimal cocycle property, in which the penalty is the infimum over all such factorizations, and show that it is equivalent to time-consistency, with the infimum attained. This holds on $L^\infty$ under continuity from below, and on $L^p$, $p<\infty$, without continuity assumptions. In the cash-additive case it reduces to the classical cocycle property. For risk measures induced by BSDEs, it represents the dynamic programming principle of a stochastic control problem whose value is the penalty.

papers.title: Simultaneous Inversion of Drift and Potential in the Fractional Magnetic Schrödinger Equation
papers.abstract: We study the Calderón problem for the fractional magnetic Schrödinger equation with drift in the bivariate additive framework. When the magnetic potential $A$ is known and fixed, we prove that the drift $b$ and the scalar potential $q$ can be simultaneously and uniquely determined from exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann measurements. When $A$ is unknown, we prove that the triple $(A,b,q)$ can only be recovered up to a natural gauge equivalence class, and that the drift $b$ is a gauge invariant, hence uniquely determined. The proofs rely on the Alessandrini identity, Runge approximation, and the unique continuation property for fractional magnetic operators. Furthermore, we have developed a numerical reconstruction framework that combines finite difference discretization, radial basis function surrogate modeling, and smoothed TV regularization. One-dimensional and two-dimensional numerical examples have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method and supported the theoretical uniqueness result.

papers.title: Independence of Thurston eigenvalues and Lyapunov exponents for quadratic rational maps
papers.abstract: We study post-critically finite quadratic rational maps $f: \mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$ where the two critical points lie in the same cycle. The Thurston eigenvalues of $f$ are those of the derivative of the Thurston pullback map $σ_f$ at its fixed point. Addressing questions of Buff--Epstein--Koch, we construct a sequence of real, bitransitive centres in the critical orbit relation curve $C_2$ which degenerates in moduli space, and whose Lyapunov exponents tend to infinity whilst the Thurston eigenvalues satisfy $\frac{1}{10}< |λ|<1$. We also show the Thurston eigenvalues across all bitransitive centres in $C_2$ have a spectral gap on compact subsets of the curve.

papers.title: Two-type thinning with alternative leader rate for random partition structures
papers.abstract: A dust-free random partition structure with infinitely many parts is a random sequence $(\mathsf{X}_1,\mathsf{X}_2,\dots)$ with $\mathsf{X}_1>\mathsf{X}_2>\dots>0$ such that $\mathsf{X}_1+\mathsf{X}_2+\dots=1$, almost surely. The Poisson-Dirichlet $\mathrm{PD}(m,0)$ distributions for $0<m<1$ are defined such that $\mathsf{X}_n = ξ_n^{-1/m}/\sum_{ν=1}^{\infty} ξ_ν^{-1/m}$, where $0<ξ_1<ξ_2<\dots$ is a homogeneous Poisson point process. It is a model for thinning invariant random partition structures, where every one of the infinitely many parts $\mathsf{X}_1,\mathsf{X}_2,\dots$ are thinned IID at rate 1. We consider a 2-type thinning where the instantaneous leader is deleted with an alternative rate $1+r\geq 0$. Then we seek time stationary random partition structures. When $r =R\in \{0,1,\dots\}$ a solution is obtained by taking $\mathrm{PD}(m,0)$ and performing ``balayage,'' where balayage means simply excavating the first $R$ points. We find the solutions for all $r \in (-1,\infty)$, which we call $\mathrm{PD}^{(r)}(m,0)$. We motivate with an application, and we present graphical representations.

papers.title: Entropic continuity of Lyapunov exponents in arbitrary dimension
papers.abstract: We prove that the sum of the positive Lyapunov exponents is entropically continuous for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism, provided the entropy exceeds its second-largest exterior growth rate. We also establish stable strong positive recurrence and show that the topological entropy is continuous, and the number of ergodic measures of maximal entropy is upper semicontinuous. This extends the result of Buzzi, Crovisier, and Sarig to arbitrary dimensions. We give examples in both the measure-theoretic and topological senses, showing that this entropy gap condition is sharp. We also present applications related to the Newhouse phenomenon and standard maps.

papers.title: Tunable Pathway Selection in Coupled Multistable Snap-Through Systems
papers.abstract: Multistable mechanical systems can store and release elastic energy through snap-through instabilities, but controlling transition pathways between stable states remains challenging when multiple routes are accessible. Here, we introduce a two-mass von Mises truss as a general model for studying pathway selection governed by coupled saddle-node bifurcations. The system consists of two coupled snap-through units with geometric imperfections, giving rise to four stable configurations: a fully inverted state, a fully natural state, and two intermediate mixed states. We show that the coupling stiffness reorganizes the quasi-static bifurcation structure and selects among three transition pathways under release: sequential snapping through one mixed state, direct cooperative snapping, or sequential snapping through the other mixed state. Using pseudo-arclength continuation, we track the relevant saddle-node bifurcations and identify the parameter regimes associated with each quasi-static pathway. We then demonstrate that dynamic bifurcation delay provides an additional rate-dependent mechanism for pathway selection. Even when the quasi-static bifurcation structure favours a unique sequential pathway, finite-rate loading delays snap-through beyond the corresponding static saddle-node points and can reorder the snapping sequence of the two units. A local reduction of the coupled dynamics near each saddle-node yields normal forms with coupling-dependent critical points and coefficients. The resulting theory identifies distinct rate-dependent delay laws in the inertia-dominated and overdamped regimes and predicts the critical rate at which the snapping order reverses. These results establish a general mechanics framework for tuning transition pathways in multistable systems through elastic coupling and loading-rate control.

papers.title: Observation delays can bias inference of selective advantage in evolutionary competition
papers.abstract: Relative-frequency trajectories are often used to infer selective advantage in competing biological populations. A common empirical approach is to fit a linear function to the logit-transformed frequency of an invading type and interpret the slope as the relative advantage. Here we test how this estimator is affected when the competing types are observed after type-specific delays. We use SARS-CoV-2 variant replacement in the United Kingdom as empirical motivation and study the mechanism with simple two-type models. In an ideal exponential replacement model, fixed or randomly distributed observation delays change the intercept of the observed log-odds trajectory but not its slope, provided that delayed counts are aggregated before frequencies are formed and boundary effects are absent. In nonlinear SIR-type models, where the relative growth is time-dependent, delays can compare the competing variants at different dynamical phases and substantially bias the fitted logit slope. This bias can occur even when the delayed replacement trajectory remains nearly linear on the logit scale. Thus, a good logistic fit to the observed data is not sufficient to guarantee that the inferred logit slope approximates well the relative growth advantage. Observation delays should therefore be accounted for when logit slopes are used as proxies for relative fitness in nonlinear evolutionary competition.

papers.title: Spectral dimension reduction of dynamical systems on graphons
papers.abstract: Spectral dimension reduction approximates a dynamical system on a large network by a low-dimensional system whose variables are weighted averages of the node states, with weights given by dominant eigenvectors of the network. Its effectiveness is closely related to the low-rank structure of the interaction matrix. We develop a graphon analogue of this reduction for dynamical systems on dense graph limits. For graphon dynamical systems, we formulate the reduction in terms of the compact self-adjoint integral operator associated with the graphon. This operator-theoretic setting gives a continuum analogue of the spectral/SVD-based framework used for finite networks: the eigenfunctions provide the reduction basis, and the decay of the corresponding singular values quantifies the effect of discarded modes. For finite-rank graphons, we prove exact reduction results for two classes of graphon dynamical systems. We also show that, for finite-rank graphons, the reduced system preserves equilibria, linear stability, and local bifurcations. For infinite-rank graphons, we derive error bounds for the spectral reduction. Numerical examples using finite-rank and infinite-rank graphons illustrate the exact and approximate regimes of the theory.

papers.title: Distribution-free testing of linear type
papers.abstract: We introduce a distribution-free goodness-of-fit test, termed the omega-1 test, which naturally complements the Kolmogorov--Smirnov test and Cramér--von Mises test and can be viewed as their (piecewise) linear analog. Defined as an $\mathrm{L}^{1}$-functional of the empirical process, the test statistic improves on balancing sensitivity to localized and diffuse alternatives and gives a robust and interpretable measure of distributional discrepancy, apart from close connections to the Wasserstein 1-distance. For finite samples, we derive a finite-dimensional computational form for the statistic under general conditions, which leads to various explicit formulas for its null distribution. Under mild continuity assumptions, the limiting statistic is distribution-free, with explicit distribution formulas. In composite settings, the statistic is also compatible with the Khmaladze transformation, enabling asymptotically distribution-free testing. The limiting transformed statistic also has an explicit distribution that escapes reliance on intractable compensator processes or purely numerical evaluation. Simulation results indicate rapid convergence of the finite-sample distributions to their limiting counterparts and support the practical applicability of the test.

papers.title: Learning Representations through Token Prediction: Geometry, Approximation, and Downstream Guarantees
papers.abstract: Token prediction is a central pre-training objective for modern language models. Despite its empirical success, why token prediction learns broadly useful representations remains incompletely understood. We develop a statistical framework connecting token prediction with representation geometry, encoder approximation, and downstream performance. Under a softmax prediction head, we show that accurate token prediction organizes token embeddings according to similarities between the distributions of contexts in which different token types appear, as measured by Hellinger distance, with explicit errors governed by prediction accuracy and token frequency. Meanwhile, the contextual representation provides a low-dimensional coordinate for the conditional distribution of the target token relative to these embeddings. We further introduce a self-consistency principle showing that repeated applications of a shared representation block can progressively refine the contextual representation without introducing additional block parameters. Among representations with the same prediction accuracy, this recurrent construction favors those that can be stably reconstructed from their contexts. Finally, we establish downstream guarantees for token generation, token community recovery, and classification by a linear probe, showing how prediction accuracy and recovered geometry translate into performance beyond the pre-training objective. Together, these results explain how the simple objective of predicting tokens can recover semantic geometry and produce broadly useful representations. A controlled simulation illustrates the theoretical mechanisms.

papers.title: Selection, Representation, and Execution in Sparse Fourier Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Sparse representations are often expected to make models smaller and also reduce inference cost. For Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs), these objectives are not equivalent or do not always align: removing parts of the learned operator can leave the underlying transforms and dense computations unchanged, while changing the grid on which the model is evaluated can introduce overhead of its own. We therefore distinguish sparsity in the representation, in the stored parameters, in the theoretical operation count, and in measured runtime, and present an empirical study of several routes toward sparse FNOs that tests each transition between them separately. Coarsening the execution grid reduces the theoretical cost without reducing measured latency, and adding a correction term recovers accuracy at the cost of making the model slower. Even an 83\% parameter reduction remains slower than the dense baseline under ordinary execution. These results motivate a stricter definition of useful sparsity: the deployed operator must preserve solution accuracy and map its reduced support to a genuinely cheaper execution path.

papers.title: An Immersed Interface Method for Parabolic Interface Problems with Nonlinear Jump Conditions
papers.abstract: We develop an immersed interface finite difference method for a one-dimensional nonlinear parabolic interface problem with jump condition \[ [u]_α=λu^+u^-. \] The method combines a Crank--Nicolson immersed interface discretization with an \(s\)-parameter reduction of the nonlinear interface condition, thereby reducing the nonlinear coupling to a scalar quadratic equation. We also discuss two different viewpoints for combining Newton iteration with immersed interface discretization, namely the IIM--Newton and Newton--IIM formulations. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the behavior and accuracy of the method.

papers.title: Multihomogeneous Measures and Stochastic Polar Representations
papers.abstract: Let \(q\in\mathbb N\), let \(G=(0,\infty)^q\), and let $ S:G\times E\longrightarrow E, (r,x)\longmapsto S_rx $ be a jointly measurable left action on an arbitrary measurable space \((E,\mathcal E)\). For \(α=(α_1,\ldots,α_q)\in(0,\infty)^q\) set $ χ_α(r)=\prod_{i=1}^q r_i^{α_i}. $ We study nonzero \(σ\)-finite measures \(ν\) satisfying $ ν(S_rA)=χ_α(r)^{-1}ν(A), r\in G, A\in\mathcal E.$ Motivated by the scalar case \(q=1\) studied in [1] we derive equivalent conditions for the existence of an \(E\)-valued random element \(Z\) such that $ ν(A) = \mathbb{E}\{\int_G\mathbb I_A(S_rZ)\prod_{i=1}^q α_i r_i^{-α_i-1}dr_i\}, A\in\mathcal E. $ We also characterise when two random elements generate the same homogeneous measure, using multihomogeneous moments and, after fixing an admissible product gauge, weighted transverse measures. When the corresponding weighted transverse measure is finite, tilting and gauge normalisation produce a canonical representer, unique in law on the prescribed gauge shell. Finally, we characterise stationarity under an action commuting with \(S\) and construct positive semidefinite tail-overlap kernels directly from \(ν\).

papers.title: Edmunds-Evans essential spectra of the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda linearization
papers.abstract: For $0<a<1$, we study the linearization $L_a$ about a smooth odd self-similar collapse profile $(Ω,c_l)$ of the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda equation, where $c_l$ is the focusing exponent. On the origin-$H^2$ realization $X=\{\varphi\in L^2(0,\infty):\varphi(0)=0,\varphi''\in L^2(0,\infty)\}$, under explicit transport, regularity, weighted-derivative, and far-field hypotheses, the first three Edmunds-Evans essential spectra are exactly the union of two possibly coincident vertical lines: $\operatorname{Re}λ=F=-1+c_l/2$ at infinity and $\operatorname{Re}λ=O=-\tilde c/2$ at the origin, where $\tilde c=c_l+a(HΩ)(0)$ and $H$ is the Hilbert transform. Off these lines, $L_a-λ$ is Fredholm, with index zero on the exterior components, $+1$ in the open strip when $F<O$, and $-1$ when $O<F$. The fourth and fifth Edmunds-Evans spectra and the Browder essential spectrum equal the closed strip. Every point of the open strip with index $+1$ is an eigenvalue. Every fixed point of the Huang-Qin-Wang-Wei positive-advection construction with $0<a<400/(848-9π^2)$, after normalization, satisfies the full hypothesis package. For all sufficiently small positive $a$, every such fixed point has $F<O$. Thus actual collapse profiles realize a nonempty Browder band. An additional kernel-nondegeneracy condition (ND) yields exact individual kernel and cokernel dimensions. We prove it outside an explicit vertical energy slab and, at sufficiently high frequency, on every closed vertical substrip of the open band separated from the far-field line. Failures in the open band are locally finite and can accumulate at high frequency only toward that line.

papers.title: Fortin operators for DPG advection discretizations
papers.abstract: We construct Fortin operators for discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin (DPG) discretizations of the advection equation with a piecewise constant divergence-free advection vector $β$, on simplicial meshes of any spatial dimension $N$ and for any polynomial degree $k \ge 1$ of the trial space. A minimal test space is built on each element from facet and interior bubbles and later augmented. The Fortin operator is shown to be bounded, uniformly over shape-regular mesh families, in the natural $β$-weighted broken test graph norm built on $L_q$ for every $1 < q < \infty$, where $q$ is the exponent conjugate to the trial exponent $p$. A non-characteristic facet condition is assumed when $k \ge 2$, while the lowest-order case requires no such condition and admits characteristic facets. As applications we prove that the practical fully discrete residual minimization method is quasioptimal in the DPG energy norm for every $1 < p < \infty$, with a quasioptimality constant governed solely by the Fortin operator, that its computable residual is a globally reliable and efficient a posteriori error estimator, and that augmenting the test space and changing the test norm improves the results in the lowest-order case.

papers.title: A note on the $Σ_2^P$-completeness of the Frobenius number
papers.abstract: Given a finite set $A$ of natural numbers whose greatest common divisor is one, the Frobenius number $g(A)$ is the largest integer that is not a non-negative integer combination of the numbers in $A$. In a 2016 preprint, Matsubara states that given $A$ and $k$, deciding if $g(A) \geq k$ is $Σ_2^P$-complete. A decade has passed since without peer-reviewed publication of this result. At the same time, the community has found it difficult to verify this result. In this note, we give a write-up of the completeness proof based on Matsubara (2016).

papers.title: Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures
papers.abstract: We study the geography of taut foliations on compact $3$-manifolds with toroidal boundary components. The central object of our work is the set of boundary multislopes realized by foliations transverse to a fixed flow on such a manifold. We prove that these sets exhibit remarkable structural properties (rationality, rigidity, and convexity) which motivate the name ziggurats. Our main tool, of independent interest, is a two-way correspondence between foliations and contact structures on $3$-manifolds with boundary: we generalize the Eliashberg-Thurston theorem, which produces pairs of positive and negative contact structures from foliations, and a construction of the first author, which builds foliations from such contact pairs. Using both directions of this correspondence, we bring contact-geometric methods to bear on the architecture of ziggurats.

papers.title: Second-Order Accuracy from Large Local Errors in Interface Problems: A Discrete Green's Function Analysis
papers.abstract: Finite difference methods for interface problems often exhibit large local truncation errors near the interface, particularly when discontinuities in coefficients or solution derivatives are present. Nevertheless, many such schemes achieve second-order accuracy, a phenomenon not fully explained by standard pointwise consistency arguments. In this work, we provide a precise explanation of this behavior through the structure of the discrete Green's function associated with the underlying conservative difference operator. An explicit representation of the Green's function reveals a two-plateau structure in its weighted increments. By expressing the numerical error in terms of this Green kernel, we show that the dominant interface truncation errors, although individually of order \(O(1)\), possess a cancellation structure that reduces their effective contribution to the global error. The exact Green's-function analysis leads to a class of conservative interface flux--balance schemes for which the cancellation mechanism yields second-order accuracy in the maximum norm. The weighted harmonic discretization is included as a particular member, and its cancellation property is established directly. For Cartesian grids with a flat interface parallel to a coordinate direction, the same conservative cancellation mechanism persists along grid lines crossing the interface. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions directly illustrate the predicted cancellation behavior and the resulting second-order accuracy. These results demonstrate that second-order accuracy in interface problems can arise from the interaction between localized truncation errors and the global structure of the discrete operator, rather than from pointwise consistency alone.

papers.title: Self-normalization for Spectral Density Integrals
papers.abstract: Integrals of spectral densities are frequently used to summarize spectral characteristics of linear processes. This work studies self-normalization for estimators of such integrals based on sequential periodograms and establishes weak convergence of the corresponding processes. For linear functionals of the spectral density, self-normalization yields pivotal limiting distributions that are free of unknown spectral quantities. For non-linear functionals, however, additional components with distinct covariance structures may arise in the limiting process. We demonstrate this phenomenon for the integrated squared spectral density.

papers.title: On the suboptimality of stochastic MPC with varying constraint horizon
papers.abstract: Enforcing stochastic state constraints over the full prediction horizon in Model Predictive Control (MPC) can be computationally demanding. Here we study stochastic MPC without terminal ingredients in which chance constraints are enforced only over a shorter constraint horizon. Using stochastic relaxed dynamic programming, we derive an explicit upper bound on the average expected closed-loop cost that depends on both prediction and constraint horizons. For linear quadratic problems with affine chance constraints and bounded uniform disturbances, we provide a deterministic reformulation via coordinate transformation and constraint tightening. Simulations illustrate the trade-off between computational effort and performance.

papers.title: Uniqueness of universal quantum dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove, under some assumptions, the uniqueness of universal quantum dimension formulae. We first show that the quantum dimensions of classical algebras have a specific form that can be represented universally, in Vogel's sense, as the product/ratio of q-dimension factors with arguments $aα+bβ+cγ$ where $c=0, 1, 2$ and $a, b$ are integers. On this basis, we derive simple uniqueness criteria, according to which all known universal quantum dimensions are unique.

papers.title: Taut foliations through a contact lens
papers.abstract: This survey explores the rich interplay between (taut) foliations and (tight) contact structures in dimension three, highlighting recent work of the author. We outline a new method for constructing taut foliations from suitable pairs of contact structures, and discuss some applications and future research directions. In particular, we give a brief account of work in progress with Jonathan Zung on ziggurats for taut foliations transverse to pseudo-Anosov flows, and we propose a (mostly speculative) contact perspective on the $L$-space conjecture.

papers.title: A variant of the block preconditioner for indefinite complex symmetric linear systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient preconditioner for solving indefinite complex symmetric linear systems within a block preconditioning framework. We analyze the convergence of the corresponding iterative method and investigate several spectral properties of the preconditioned matrix, including eigenvalue distributions and eigenvector structures. The new preconditioner is used to accelerate the convergence of the flexible version of GMRES. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed preconditioner, and comparisons with existing block preconditioners demonstrate its superior performance.

papers.title: On Cauchy Problems for Parabolic Equations with Rough Coefficients
papers.abstract: The presented work investigates the Cauchy problems for parabolic equations in both non-divergence and divergence forms with rough diffusion coefficients, which commonly arise in composite media, financial pricing, and viscous fluids. Under critical regularity settings, we establish the unique solvability in optimal fractional Sobolev spaces. The first key technical step lies in constructing an effective approximation scheme with truncated and mollified diffusion coefficients $a^ε(t,x)$, for which we rigorously prove the uniform preservation of high-frequency smallness. By incorporating this approximation scheme with paraproduct decomposition, Fefferman-Stein maximal inequalities, Coifman-Meyer bilinear estimates, and refined Sobolev embeddings, we close the uniform a priori estimates and then pass to the limit. Furthermore, we prove that the threshold $s < \frac{1}{2}$ is sharp by constructing explicit counterexamples. These theoretical results provide a rigorous mathematical framework in the study of Cauchy problems for parabolic equations with rough coefficients.

papers.title: Sylvester's four point problem for ball-convex bodies
papers.abstract: We investigate Sylvester's classical four-point problem for ball-convex bodies, where convex hulls are replaced by intersections of balls of a fixed radius $R$. We show that the Efron--Buchta identities persist in this framework, so that the distribution of the number of vertices of the $R$-ball-convex hull of $n$ uniform random points is determined by the moments of the volumes of the hulls of its subsamples, and vice versa. For three and four uniform random points in an arbitrary planar ball-convex body, we determine the Sylvester probabilities of the $R$-ball-convex hull. We also give an extension of Groemer's inequality for the expected area of the ball-convex hull of $n$ random points and show that it is minimised by the disc of the same area. In particular, this yields an isoperimetric inequality for the ball-convex analogue of the affine length of the boundary curve. For the unit disc, we can express the Sylvester probabilities using dilogarithmic functions of the radius $R$, and give explicit values at $R=1$. As $R\to\infty$, these recover the classical Sylvester probabilities. As another consequence, we determine the exact distribution function of the circumradius of three uniform random points in he disc on $[1,\infty)$.

papers.title: Cramér transform, half-space depth and threshold phenomena for convex bodies
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between the Cramér transform and Tukey's half-space depth for log-concave probability measures. For the uniform probability measure $μ_K$ on a convex body $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, we prove the sharp pointwise comparison $$Λ_K^*(x)\leq -\log q_K(x)\leq Λ_K^*(x)+\frac12\log n+C,\qquad x\in\operatorname{int}(K),$$ where $C$ is an absolute constant. The order $\log n$ is optimal, as shown by the Euclidean ball. The proof combines exponential tilting, one-dimensional log-concavity, and self-concordance of the Cramér transform. As consequences, we obtain sharp-order moment and tail estimates for $Λ_K^*$ and identify $\exp(Λ_K^*(x))$, up to polynomial factors in the dimension, with the number of independent samples needed for $x$ to be captured by their random convex hull. We also establish an $O(n^2)$ variance bound for the logarithmic half-space depth and use it to derive a general criterion for sharp thresholds of random convex hulls. In particular, this criterion applies to the uniform measures on $\ell_p$-balls for every $p>1$. These results establish a quantitative link between large-deviation cost, geometric depth, and sampling complexity in high-dimensional convex geometry.

papers.title: Nijenhuis torsion and Frölicher-Nijenhuis brackets of recursion operators via their full-fledged forms
papers.abstract: We present a novel approach to computing the Nijenhuis torsion and Frölicher-Nijenhuis brackets of recursion operators for symmetries, based on their full-fledged forms introduced by Jahnová and Vojčák (2024). In contrast to the conventional approach, which represents recursion operators as maps between shadows of nonlocal symmetries within a given covering, our method allows the Nijenhuis torsion to be computed directly from its defining formula, without requiring any additional mathematical constructions. The same framework can also be used to compute the Frölicher-Nijenhuis bracket of recursion operators and to verify their compatibility directly in their full-fledged forms. The procedure is illustrated by several examples of full-fledged recursion operators for symmetries of differential equations in four independent variables, including a new recursion operator for the four-dimensional universal hierarchy equation that, to the best of our knowledge, has not previously appeared in the literature. A notable feature of this new full-fledged recursion operator is that its shadow component does not appear to admit a reasonable representation in any of the standard conventional forms. Nevertheless, our approach allows us to prove directly that the Nijenhuis torsion of this operator vanishes. For the examples considered, the corresponding Frölicher-Nijenhuis brackets also vanish, confirming the compatibility of the respective pairs of recursion operators. This demonstrates that full-fledged forms provide an effective framework for studying the hereditary and compatibility properties of recursion operators, including highly nonlocal and/or multidimensional cases that are difficult to handle by existing methods.

papers.title: Equilibrium fluctuations of the weakly asymmetric inclusion process
papers.abstract: We prove that the stationary density fluctuation field of the one-dimensional weakly asymmetric simple inclusion process converges to the energy solution of the stochastic Burgers equation. The key technical ingredient is a second-order Boltzmann-Gibbs principle tailored to the microscopic current. As a consequence, we also obtain Ornstein-Uhlenbeck fluctuations for the symmetric inclusion process in a weakly condensing regime, a result of independent interest.

papers.title: Solute dispersion in magnetically influenced multiphase flow through a porous tube: axial transport and microrotational effects
papers.abstract: This study presents a theoretical investigation of generalized solute dispersion in magnetohydrodynamic multiphase tube flow with porous layers. A two-fluid analytical model is developed for applications in biofluid and environmental fluid dynamics. The model comprises a micropolar (non-Newtonian) fluid core representing the rotational behaviour of red blood cells and a Newtonian plasma periphery embedded with Brinkman and Darcy porous structures, corresponding to the glycocalyx and endothelial layers with distinct permeability characteristics. A transverse magnetic field is incorporated to investigate how magnetic-field-induced modifications of the carrier flow influence solute localisation, with potential relevance to magnetic nanoparticle-mediated drug delivery. Using the generalised dispersion framework of Sankarasubramanian & Gill, analytical solutions are derived to investigate how the coupled axial velocity field and associated microrotational dynamics influence solute transport. The analytical predictions are independently validated through Brownian dynamics simulations, demonstrating excellent agreement for the temporal evolution of the zeroth and first transport moments. The results reveal the previously unexplored influence of microrotational dynamics on solute concentration, convection coefficients and effective dispersion, providing new insights into the coupled roles of translational and rotational fluid motion in biofluid transport. This work bridges an important gap in the literature and establishes a generalized theoretical framework linking magnetic fields, micropolar fluids and porous arterial structures for biofluid transport, targeted drug delivery and clinical engineering applications.

papers.title: Sharp Singularity-Degree Bounds for Equality-Generated SDP-RLT Relaxations of Binary Programs
papers.abstract: Singularity degree is an important measure of semidefinite programming (SDP) degeneracy, but it is generally unavailable a priori from the problem data. We augment the Shor relaxation of nonempty binary sets $\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:Ax=b\}$ with the first-level Reformulation-Linearization Technique (RLT) equations generated by the defining linear equalities. For the resulting equality-generated SDP-RLT relaxation, we determine the exact worst-case singularity degree. If $\operatorname{rank}(A)=m$ and $0<m<n$, then the associated relaxation has singularity degree at most $\min\{m,n-m\}$, and this rank-nullity bound is attained for every possible rank in this range. Consequently, the worst-case singularity degree over this class is $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ for $n\geq 2$. This is strikingly smaller than the sharp general bound $n$ for feasible SDP systems with matrix variables of order $n+1$ (Sturm, 2000, Example 2). Thus, for individual relaxations, rank and nullity provide an a priori bound on the otherwise inaccessible singularity degree and on the Hölder exponent in error bounds estimating distance to feasibility from constraint residuals.

papers.title: Failure of a Brunn-Minkowski-type inequality for the Gaussian torsional rigidity
papers.abstract: Let $u$ be the torsion function for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator on a bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n$, i.e., the solution of $Δu - x \cdot \nabla u = -1$ in $Ω$ with $u = 0$ on $\partialΩ$. Let $T_γ(Ω) = \int_Ωu \, dγ$ be the Gaussian torsional rigidity. We prove that the Brunn-Minkowski-type inequality $T_γ((1-t)Ω_0 + tΩ_1)^α \le (1-t) T_γ(Ω_0)^α + t T_γ(Ω_1)^α$ fails for every exponent $α> 0$ and in every dimension $n \ge 2$, for a pair of convex bodies centrally symmetric with respect to the origin, which may be taken smooth with positive curvature. This answers Conjecture 1.4 for any $n \geq 2$, and Question~(Q), of Marín Sola and Salerno in the negative. The mechanism is a first-order lower bound for $T_γ$ at a ball $Ω_0$ under Minkowski perturbations. When the perturbing body $Ω_1$ has small torsion and large mean width, $T_γ((1-t)Ω_0 + tΩ_1)$ increases to first order. Since the Minkowski combination has larger torsion than both endpoints, no exponent can repair the inequality. For $n=1$, convexity with the optimal exponent $1/3$ holds on symmetric intervals by results of the same authors, \cite{MSS26}. We prove that the logarithm of the torsion is neither convex nor concave along Minkowski combinations of symmetric intervals, that no non-zero exponent yields concavity, and that convexity fails for every positive exponent when one set is a union of two intervals or when the sets are reflected off-center intervals.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the site-percolation analogues of the Easo-Severo-Tassion cutset theorems
papers.abstract: Easo, Severo and Tassion [EST25] proved two theorems about minimal edge cutsets in infinite graphs: that non-triviality of the uniform critical percolation parameter is equivalent to exponential growth of the number of minimal edge cutsets of size n separating a vertex from infinity, and that uniform transience is an alternative sufficient assumption. We show that the naive extensions of (the original contribution to) these theorems to site percolation and vertex cutsets are false; our counterexample involves modifying a rooted binary tree and replacing edges with gadgets that allow many choices for where to block (in constructing a cutset) one of two local routes, while keeping every vertex uniformly close to a supercritical, uniformly transient shortcut skeleton.

papers.title: Exact Entanglement Swapping through Single-Occupancy Measurements in Gaussian Fermion States
papers.abstract: We determine the exact entanglement structure of the conditional state obtained by measuring $m$ corresponding rungs ($m\leq N/2$) in two identical copies of an arbitrary half-filled free fermion Gaussian state and post-selecting the same normalized single-fermion state ($|ψ\rangle = u|10\rangle+v|01\rangle$, where 0 and 1 denote the fermion occupancy on each sites) on each rung. For $m<N/2$, the conditional wavefunction generally depends on the initial state. Nevertheless, whenever the selected outcome has nonzero probability, the state on the unmeasured sites remains Gaussian and factorizes exactly into $N-m$ different orthogonal modes including $m$ inter-copy entangling modes and $N-2m$ spectator modes localized in one copy. Consequently, the entanglement entropy between the unmeasured parts of the two copies is $S=m h_2(|v|^2)$, independent of the initial state, where $h_2(x)=-x\ln x-(1-x)\ln(1-x)$. The success probability is given by $P_m=\det C_L\det(I_m-C_L)=\det(C_{LR}C_{RL})$, determined solely by the initial correlations and independent of ($u$,$v$). Equal-weight Bell post-selection serves as a special case that achieves the maximal entanglement swapping.

papers.title: Advancements in Spectral Collocation Methods for High-Order Eigenvalue Problems
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on computing spectral solutions for high-order eigenvalue problems using an efficient discretization method based on Chebfun spectral discretization algorithms and domain truncation. We solve several numerical eigenvalue problems, demonstrating both the accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed approach.

papers.title: A partial data coefficient identification inverse problem for a semilinear damped wave operator
papers.abstract: This manuscript deals with a coefficient identification inverse problem for a semilinear damped wave operator in a bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^{1+d}\ (d\geq 2)$. We establish the unique recovery of the damping coefficient, zeroth-order linear term, and the coefficient of the power-type nonlinearity from the partial Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. We investigate the corresponding uniqueness problem under the assumption that the coefficients are known in a neighborhood of the boundary, while the Neumann boundary data are prescribed only on an arbitrarily small open subset of the boundary. The analysis is largely based on the unique continuation principle, Fourier Analysis and the higher-order linearization technique.

papers.title: Proof of the planar Khavinson-Shapiro conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded domain whose boundary is a finite union of pairwise disjoint Jordan curves. We prove the planar Khavinson--Shapiro conjecture in this setting: if every polynomial on $\mathbb{R}^2$ agrees on $\partialΩ$ with a harmonic polynomial, then $\partialΩ$ is an ellipse and $Ω$ is its bounded interior.

papers.title: Finite Sample Identification of Analytic Nonlinear Systems
papers.abstract: This paper studies the identification of linearly parameterized nonlinear (LPN) systems. Although LPN systems share the same linear parameterization structure as linear systems, they are more challenging to identify. In particular, previous work has shown, through a counterexample based on a piecewise-affine system, that non-active exploration is generally insufficient for LPN system identification. In this paper, we consider LPN systems with real-analytic feature functions. We show that non-active exploration is sufficient for the identification of this class of systems by establishing non-asymptotic convergence rates of least-squares estimation and set-membership estimation. In addition, we provide counterexamples to show that non-active exploration may not be sufficient for system identification for non-real-analytic systems, even if those systems are infinitely differentiable. We present numerical experiments to further support and validate our theoretical results.

papers.title: Multiple Nonlinear Waves by (Quantum) Neural Networks: Checking the AI supremacy
papers.abstract: To test the potential of so-called quantum physics-informed neural network (QPINN) technology for solving evolutionary partial differential equations, we consider the problem of multiple wave propagation in a weakly nonlinear medium described by the Korteweg-de Vries equation with periodic boundary conditions. Although this problem is solvable analytically, high-genus solutions could represent a rather challenging testbed for numerical methods. Therefore, our idea is to test whether a QPINN is sufficiently mature for application in this context by providing a set of indicators of merit and performing several numerical experiments.

papers.title: Discontinuous phase transitions in the one-dimensional pair and triplet creation processes
papers.abstract: Dickman and Tomé (1991) introduced models on $Z$ in which $k$ consecutive occupied sites give birth at rate $λ$, individual particles die at rate 1, and the configuration is subject to nearest neighbor stirring. They claimed that the pair creation model ($k=2$) has a continuous phase transition and was in the universality class of directed percolation, but the triplet creation model ($k=3$) has a discontinuous (or first-order) phase transition when the stirring rate is large. Hinrichsen (2000a) disputed the second claim and argued that first-order phase transitions in 1+1-dimensional nonequilibrium systems with fluctuating ordered phases are impossible. In this paper we prove rigorously that the phase transitions are discontinuous in both the pair and triplet models when the stirring rate is large. At the end of Section 2 we state some open problems and suggest reasons that the results in the physics literature differ from those presented here,

papers.title: High-order energy-stable BGN parametric finite element methods for geometric flows
papers.abstract: We construct high-order Runge--Kutta extensions of Barrett--Garcke--Nürnberg (BGN) parametric finite element methods for curve-shortening flow and curve diffusion of planar curves and for mean curvature flow and surface diffusion of closed genus-$0$ surfaces. On each time slab $I_m=(t_m,t_{m+1}]$, the continuous equations are posed on the left-endpoint surface $Γ^m=Γ^{t_m}$ through the map $\X^{m,t}:Γ^m\toΓ^t$, whose target is the evolving surface at time $t$. For curves, this formulation follows by harmonic pullback from $Γ^0$ to $Γ^m$. For surfaces, an orientation-preserving harmonic diffeomorphism is posed separately on each time slab, and conformality yields the weight $\frac12|\nabla_{Γ^m}\X^{m,t}|^2$. Evaluating the time-slab equations at the Runge--Kutta internal times and applying mass-lumped parametric finite elements yields systems on the common domain $Γ^m$, with $Γ^{t_m+c_iτ_m}$ as the intermediate target geometry. This internal-time discretization constructs high-order BGN-structured extensions for the four flows. For an algebraically stable tableau with nonnegative weights, every exact stage solution with nondegenerate intermediate configurations satisfies monotone decay of the discrete curve length or surface area for every positive time step for which that solution exists. Radau IIA experiments exhibit energy decay for all four flows and BGN-type mesh redistribution in the curve tests.
